items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I used to play, toured with Bobby Womack as well.

ctx.x: We were talking about charts or playing by ear.

Oh yeah. So he did, we had twelve tunes we were going to record. And he’d done charts for six horns. There was two trumpets, a bone, and three saxes. So we were rehearsing them in the studio and they were great. Like they were fun man, and they were voiced great, this guy could write really nice. And then Buddy Miles would show up at the studio, three hours late, and he’d go, “Hey let me hear what you got for this tune.” And we would play it and he goes, “well that’s cool but I kind of hear this.” And then he…

concentrate on playing the show and it was great. And thinking on my feet if something changes. What if he goes to the bridge four bars early like he would on a regular basis. I’m not buried in a chart and in the wrong place. I’m going, he’s going to the bridge, you know.
